Good to know This operator's manual documents the automation components BendMaster (60) and BendMaster (150) in the TruBend Cell 5000 bending cell for the automatic handling of sheets on the press brakes of the TruBend Series 5000. The machine documentation includes: ■ Spare parts catalog. ■ Schematic. ■ TruBend Series 5000 operator's manual. ■ TruTops Bend software manual. ■ Operator's manual ToolMaster (Option) KB37. 1. Safety concept The "Safety" chapter describes the safety concept of the machine. It specifies the guards and the manufacturer's design measures for safe operation of the machine. It points out dangers when handling the machine and specifies measures taken by the user to avoid possible dangers. The "Hazards" section is based on the manufacturer's risk assessment and describes the residual risk. The user must take measures to prevent the hazards. The measures must comply with the national safety and accident prevention regulations of the country in which the machine is operated. Dangerous points on the machine are marked with warning signs and information plates. The operator's manual contains warnings, which warn of dan- gers and specify measures to avoid these dangers. Warnings have the following structure: ■ The signal word designates the degree of a danger. ■ The danger description specifies the danger and possible consequences if attention is not paid to the danger. ■ The measures for prevention of the danger are planned. Example of a warning: Risk of fatal injury due to falling load! Ø Observe the safety regulations for handling heavy loads. Ø Never walk under a suspended load. Ø Use certified tackle and means of transportation of sufficient size. Ø Employ qualified personnel to transport the machine. Ø Carry out transport in accordance with the transport regula- tions. A warning contains signaling words that are explained in the fol- lowing table: Signal word Description DANGER If the dangerous situation is not prevented, death or serious injuries will result. WARNING If the dangerous situation is not prevented, death or serious injuries could result. 1‐4 Safety concept 2023-05-01 B1164en Safety chapter Warning sign and information plates Warnings DANGER

2. Regulations and guidelines TRUMPF issues an EU declaration of conformity for the hydraulic press brake in accordance with EC Machinery Direc- tive 2006/42/EC. The hydraulic press brake machine is a com- plete machine. The standards applied by TRUMPF are stated in the EU declaration of conformity supplied. With the CE marking, TRUMPF confirms compliance with the fol- lowing EU directives: ■ EC Machinery directive 2006/42/EC. ■ Directive regarding electromagnetic compatibility 2014/30/EU. The CE marking is on the nameplate. TRUMPF issues a declaration of conformity for the hydraulic press brake in accordance with the British Machinery Directive. The hydraulic press brake is a complete machine. The stand- ards applied by TRUMPF are stated in the declaration of con- formity supplied. With the UKCA marking, TRUMPF confirms compliance with the following directives: ■ Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 No. 1597. ■ Electromagnetic Compatibility Regulations 2016 No. 1091. The UKCA marking is on the nameplate. The machine meets the requirements of ANSI B11.3. 1‐6 Regulations and guidelines 2023-05-01 B1164en Laws and guidelines in the EU Regulations and guidelines in UK Laws and guidelines in the USA

4. Laser classes Beam sources, which emit laser radiation are divided into laser classes according to international standard IEC 60825-1 (USA: ANSI Z136.1, ANSI B11.21). The laser class corresponds to the hazard level of the laser light emitted. All beam sources which the personnel can come into contact with are listed below. In addition, other beam sources can be installed which emit laser radiation (for example, light barriers, for component and container query). However, personnel are not exposed to this radiation at any time during operation or during setting and main- tenance work. Laser class Description Beam source on the machine 1 The accessible laser radiation is not dangerous under normal, foreseeable conditions. – 1M The accessible laser radiation lies in the visible spectral range of 302.5 nm to 4000 nm. The accessible laser radiation is not dangerous for the eye as long as the cross section is not reduced using optical instruments (magnifying glasses, lenses, telescopes). – 2 The accessible laser radiation lies in the visible spectral range (400 nm to 700 nm). There is no danger to the eyes when the exposure time is limited (up to 0.25 s). Additional radiation parts outside the wavelength spectrum of 400-700 nm fulfill the conditions of class 1. The eyes are normally protected against laser radiation by turn- ing away and closing the eyelids. 3R Diode lasers on the sheet sensor for height measure- ment Wavelength 450 nm. 2M The accessible laser radiation lies in the visible spectral range of 400 nm to 700 nm. There is no danger to the eyes in the case of short exposure time (up to 0.25 s) as long as the laser beam is not observed through optical instruments (magni- fying glass, lens, telescope). Additional radiation components outside the wavelength spectrum of 400-700 nm meet the con- ditions of class 1M. The eyes are normally protected against laser radiation by turn- ing away and closing the eyelids. – 3R The accessible laser radiation is in the wavelength spectrum of 302.5 nm to 10 6 nm and is hazardous to the eye. The power/ energy is max. 5x the limit value of the permissible class 2 laser radiation in the wavelength range from 400 nm to 700 nm. – 3B The accessible laser radiation is very dangerous to the eyes and also to the skin. Looking into the laser beam of class 3B lasers directly is dan- gerous. The accessible laser radiation from class 3B laser products can damage the skin if the maximum permissible exposure val- ues are exceeded. – 1‐8 Laser classes 2023-05-01 B1164en

5. Operational safety The machine can result in the following dangers if it is used inappropriately or for purposes other than those intended, or else if it is not safe to operate: ■ Dangers to the safety of the personnel. ■ Damage to the machine and other material assets of the user. 5.1 Intended use The user may use the machine only in the industrial sector. Installation, operating and transport conditions defined by TRUMPF must be adhered to and maintenance work must be carried out in accordance with the Operator's manual. The user must observe the regulations of the country in which the machine is being operated as well as national and regional safety and accident prevention regulations. The user can transport cold sheets using the machine and posi- tion them for machining. The following is not permitted: ■ Unauthorized alteration or conversion of the machine by the user or personnel. ■ Any working procedure that impairs the safety. ■ Processing of hot, splintering or brittle materials. ■ Use of tools from other manufacturers without release by TRUMPF. ■ The machining of scarred or sandblasted sheets (does not apply to machining using the pivoting-jaw gripper). ■ Exceeding the maximum workpiece dimensions. ■ Exceeding the maximum workpiece weight. ■ Exceeding the maximum load capacity (workpiece and grip- per weight). The handling equipment is used to load and unload a bending cell. The following types of processing are prohibited with the han- dling equipment: ■ Exceeding the max. conveying weight. ■ Use of pallets other than Europallet 1200 x 800 mm. Any use going beyond this is considered to be unauthorized use. TRUMPF is not liable for any damage, especially personal 1‐10 Operational safety 2023-05-01 B1164en Machine BendMaster handling equipment (option) Disclaimer

injury and damage to property as well as production failures resulting from this. The risk is borne solely by the user. The war- ranty will be voided. If the operating company modifies or converts the machine, the operating company becomes solely responsible for the safety of the machine and not TRUMPF. 5.2 Significant change to the machine The machine will be supplied as a complete machine. The machine is operationally safe at the time of commissioning. The user can produce goods with the machine as intended. After commissioning, the responsibility for the safety of the machine is transferred from the manufacturer to the user. The machine has been significantly changed if a new hazard is posed by this change, which results in an increase in an exist- ing risk or to a new risk which cannot be eliminated or reduced with simple guards. Simple guards in the aforementioned context include guards which are integrated in the safety circuit of the machine via sig- nal exchange or which shut down or shield dangerous machine functions. The machine can be optionally equipped with signal and safety interfaces ex works, which make it possible for the user or an integrator to add components to the machine, e.g. a robot or fixture or to integrate the machine in a superordinate system. The user or integrator is responsible for the safety of the altered machine: ■ Integration may only be performed by qualified personnel. ■ Connection of components to the interfaces must be per- formed according to the specification set out by TRUMPF. ■ Personnel must not be endangered by components inte- grated in the machine. ■ National regulations must be observed. If the user or integrator has made a significant change to the machine, they become the manufacturer of the altered machine. The user or integrator must carry out an evaluation process (e.g. a CE conformity assessment procedure) for the altered machine in accordance with national regulations (e.g. the EC Machinery Directive). He, as the manufacturer, is responsible for the safety of the significantly changed machine. B1164en 2023-05-01 Operational safety 1‐11 Delivery condition Significant change Conformity evaluation

6. Hazards The "Hazards" section is based on the manufacturer's risk assessment and describes the residual risk. The user must take measures to prevent the hazards. 6.1 Mechanical dangers Dangers due to floating loads The BendMaster moves with suspended loads during loading and unloading. Note Always wear safety shoes in the working area. Unexpected vacuum loss in case of a suctioned workpiece! Risk of fatal injury due to workpiece crashing! Ø No permanent workplace is permitted outside the safety fencing within the swivel range of the BendMaster. Ø Follow the safety regulations for handling heavy loads. Ø Do not enter the danger zone when a workpiece is attached by suction. Ø Do not fail to follow any of the following instructions. ■ Never manually guide a load suspended from the BendMaster out of the danger zone or manually guide it into the danger zone. ■ In the event of a power failure: − Wait until the power supply has been restored. − Securely deposit the workpiece on a pallet. ■ If there is a defect directly at the BendMaster that requires repair work in the danger zone: − Secure the suspended load from above using a crane and remove it. or − Drop the suspended load with the safety doors closed before entering the danger zone. B1164en 2023-05-01 Hazards 1‐13 DANGER In manual and automatic mode

■ If there is a defect to the system outside the danger zone: − Eliminate the defect. − Deposit the suspended load on a pallet. ■ Do not move the BendMaster with suspended loads into the home position in order to enter the danger zone afterwards. Set down the workpiece first. In manual mode (for example, teach mode), the operator may be within the safety fencing to move the axes of the robot and the press brake. If the compressed air fails, an error message is displayed in manual mode and the system stops. If these error messages are acknowledged, the system will still run in order to put the workpiece down. It will also emit an audible warning signal and display a message on the HMI. Unexpected drop in pressure at the gripper of the BendMaster while a workpiece is clamped! Risk of injury due to workpiece falling down. Ø If an acoustic warning signal is emitted, exit the processing cell immediately and close the safety doors. Ø Acknowledge messages. Ø Also during maintenance and cleaning work before entering the safety cabin: move the BendMaster manually and set down the clamped workpiece safely. Pressure drop at the BendMaster gripper while a workpiece is clamped caused by switching off the compressed air supply. Risk of injury due to workpiece falling down. Ø Only turn off theMAIN SWITCH and the compressed air supply if no workpiece is gripped on the BendMaster's vac- uum gripper. The safety doors are not monitored in manual mode. Risk of injury and damage to property due to suspended load in manual mode. Ø Move the BendMaster only if no other persons are in the danger zone. Ø Only perform overhead movements with suspended loads from a safe distance. Ø Make sure that the suspended load does not collide with the safety fencing or other parts in the danger zone. 1‐14 Hazards 2023-05-01 B1164en Additionally, in manual mode WARNING WARNING WARNING

■ Do not modify automatically generated traverse points such that the risk of workpiece loss is increased. Danger due to increased movement dynamics (productivity package) All BendMaster systems (KB36) are delivered with increased movement dynamics (productivity package). Increased movement dynamics due to productivity package The workpiece may fall out or be ejected! Risk of injury! Ø Before starting an older project, check the holding force and stability of the corresponding gripper and confirm the respec- tive dialog. Ø Calculate the suction cup capacity . Ø Adapt the number of suction cups to the gripper. Ø If the number of suction cups cannot be increased: reduce the speed of the travel points (see "Points, editing", pg. 4 ‐98). Ø For magnet gripper: reduce the BendMaster speed (over- ride) to 50% . Dangers due to unexpected movements Unexpected movements of the robot! Risk of crushing. Ø When working inside the safety cabin: Maintain a sufficient distance from moving assemblies. Ø Do not stand under the BendMaster. Organizational measures to be taken by the user The user must take the following measures before starting work- ing on the machine: ■ Perform a risk assessment in accordance with national regu- lations. To create the risk assessment the section "Dangers" and all warnings in the operator's manual must be taken into account. ■ Define which personnel are responsible for safety, operation, maintenance, setting work and service. ■ Provide personal protective equipment (for example, protec- tive gloves, safety shoes, hearing protection, safety glasses). 8.1 Training and instructing operators The user must take the following measures before the personnel start working on the machine: ■ Inform personnel about possible dangers and safety meas- ures. Chapter 1 "Safety" forms the basis. ■ Personnel are obligated to read the technical documentation of the machine. Recommendation: obtain written confirma- tion from the personnel. ■ Instruct personnel that warnings and warning signs are to be observed. ■ Ensure personnel wear personal protective equipment (for example, protective gloves, safety shoes, hearing protection, safety glasses). 8.2 Due diligence when operating the machine The user is obligated to ensure the operational safety of the machine according to national regulations. Among others, the fol- lowing measures must be taken: ■ Ensure that only authorized personnel works at the machine. ■ Ensure that maintenance work is carried out according to the prescribed intervals. ■ Ensure that regular visual inspections are carried out on components that could jeopardize operational safety if dam- aged (e.g. hydraulic system hoses, pressure containers, etc.). ■ Make sure that damaged or missing warning signs on the machine are replaced. 4.2 Power supply Residual current device (RCD) Notes ■ Whether a residual current circuit breaker has to be used depends on the local electricity company. ■ On the line side, only residual current circuit breakers of type B (sensitive to all types of fault current, EN 50178/5.2.11.2; VDE 0160) are approved. A fault current circuit breaker provides protection from fault cur- rents due to directly or indirectly touching live parts. If a fault current circuit breaker is used to provide protection from direct contact, an isolating transformer must be used (EN 50178 section 5.2.11.1, VDE 0160). This is because the leakage current resulting from the design is >30 mA. If a fault current circuit breaker is to be used to provide protec- tion from indirect contact, this must be selected depending on the machine's fault current. Note In rare cases, user-side voltage fluctuations on the machine's power input filter may lead to higher leakage currents than the typically specified value. The main power supply system and the machine must then be separated by an isolating transformer. Typical leakage currents are 300 mA. 1. Machine concept Within the TruBend Cell 5000 bending cell, the bending process at the press brake can be performed fully automatically using the BendMaster handling system. The BendMaster has the fol- lowing features: ■ Four rotational axes and a linear axis as floor lane ■ Sheet sensor for workpiece recognition. ■ Offline programming with TruTops Bend. ■ Very high flexibility thanks to the option of configuring the loading and unloading places, the length of the floor lane, gripper changes and the regripping station as desired, as well as thanks to a sheet removal station for small parts automation and conveyor belts for transfer out of the cell. ■ Suitable both for automatic, unattended operation as well as for manual operation with BendMaster in the home position and with the safety fencing closed. ■ BendMaster (60) or BendMaster (150) for different load capacities. 3‐4 Machine concept 2023-05-01 B1164en

The arm is moved by the rail interpola- tion of three drives. Turned away from the press brake, the arm is used to load and unload the BendMaster. The controllers for the servo drives and an industrial PC are in the electrical cabinet. This industrial PC controls the drive axes and evaluates the data of the sheet sensor. The industrial PC is connected to the manual control unit and the press brake in real time and linked to the BendMaster stationary electrical cabinet. 3.5 Sheet sensor The BendMaster is operated with a sheet sensor used to iden- tify the position of the workpieces. The sensor head consists of 2 CMOS cameras (coarse and fine position recognition), 4 LED modules for illumination of the work- piece and a cross laser module for height measurement. The images are evaluated by an industrial PC in the electrical cabinet of the BendMaster. The sheet sensor performs the following three functions one after another: ■ Rough recognition of the workpiece stack. ■ Height measurement of the workpiece stack. ■ Fine recognition of the workpiece. The camera takes a picture of the pallet with workpiece stacks. It may be composed of several individual images. The function lighting of the BendMaster is used for this purpose. CAD data of the workpiece is saved in the computer. This data is used to create reference models. The respective pattern is searched for in the recorded image and the position of the work- piece is determined if the pattern is found. This position data is used to bring the sensor head into the right position for height measurement and/or fine position recognition of the workpiece. The rough recognition process only has to be performed once for each loading cycle, since the pallet with the workpiece stacks can no longer be moved after loading the bending cell. The precise distance between the workpiece and the gripper must be determined. The laser module projects a cross into the field of view of the camera for this purpose. The distance is then calculated using a triangulation method. The height of each workpiece stack is measured once by default. The BendMaster automatically calculates the height of the remaining workpiece stack since it knows the sheet thick- ness of the workpiece. The height of the workpiece stack can be measured after every xth workpiece. Potential errors due to inaccuracies of the sheet thickness are compensated for in this way. The precise position of the workpiece is determined (±0.2 mm) in order to position the gripper properly. To avoid daylight influen- ces, narrowband flash lighting (blue LEDs) is used for the fine recognition process. 3‐8 The most important assemblies 2023-05-01 B1164en Sensor head Signal processor Sheet sensor functions Rough recognition of the workpiece stack Height measurement of the workpiece stack Fine recognition of the workpiece

This process can be carried out twice at different points of long components to minimize angle errors. After it has been positioned precisely, the workpiece can be picked up with the gripper. 3.6 Rotational transformer A continuous rotational transformer is integrated in the D axis, which allows the D axis to be rotated without an end position. For this reason or other reasons, the BendMaster may pick up two or more work- pieces at the same time. Two systems are available to prevent this: ■ Double sheet recognition ■ Double sheet separation Double sheet recognition The double sheet recognition process is performed by means of three sensors in the C arm of the BendMaster. When a part is picked up, its weight is measured and compared with the reference value from TruTops Bend. Each time a workpiece is picked up by the BendMaster, its weight is measured and compared to the reference value so that it does not go unnoticed if a double-sheet is picked up. The minimum permissible weight of a sheet is 400 g. Double sheet separation If several workpieces are picked up by the BendMaster, they can be separated mechanically by the double sheet separation system. The gripper is used to bend the workpieces. The workpieces bend easily, however the degree of bending is always within the elastic range. This bending process exerts a force on the two workpieces, resulting in a peeling effect. 5. Industry 4.0 with TruConnect 5.1 What is Industry 4.0 at TRUMPF? Industry 4.0 is the digital networking of production in the Smart Factory. It has the objective of increasing overall productivity, flexibility and process stability and to create company-wide value- adding networks. The central requirement for this is that the dif- ferent systems and machines in the production network can com- municate with one another. To do this, they must understand each other's languages and be able to interpret the signals received. There are interfaces to make this possible. Interfaces define the content of the signals and allow the data to be interpreted, even if it was sent from another system. In order that the sent data can be used as effectively as possi- ble, one requires intelligent systems which can evaluate the data and can derive and execute the corresponding measures from this. Such systems could be, e.g., ERP/PPC systems for production control or also monitoring systems, which monitor certain states and react autonomously, as required. The systems can be utilized both locally in the company as well as online via internet-based services and platforms. With TruConnect, TRUMPF provides both the necessary interfa- ces for networking as well as the systems for evaluation and control – offline and online. The systems which TruConnect contains are distributed over the following areas: ■ Production overview ■ Production control ■ Connectivity ■ Remote Support 5.2 Production overview Machine data is acquired and analyzed with Oseon Analytics. If an idle state or malfunction should occur, the software will pro- vide information about the causes via e-mail or text message. These can be remedied quickly, thereby reducing the idle times. The entire machine park can be monitored in real time with Oseon Analytics. 3‐32 Industry 4.0 with TruConnect 2023-05-01 B1164en Industry 4.0 Interfaces Systems for data evaluation TruConnect Production areas Oseon Analytics

Example Fig. 78487 5.3 Production control Oseon includes various functions which build on each other as configuration stages Oseon Go, Oseon Grow and Oseon Flow. Thanks to the extensive functions for managing stock, material and customer data, and offers and orders, small companies can manage and control nearly their entire workflow with the func- tions of Oseon. Thus, in some cases, an expensive and often over-dimensioned ERP/PPC system can be done without, or an existing ERP/PPC system can be sensibly supplemented. The following functions are available, which differ according to configuration stage: ■ Oseon Analytics: Overview and evaluation of data sent by individual workstations (online via myTRUMPF). ■ Oseon Preparation: Work preparations, production planning, production control. ■ Oseon Fabrication: Support and coordination of production. Note The Telepresence Box is the sole physical interface between the machine and the customer network. All data (e.g. OPC UA, condition monitoring, production orders for Oseon, remote support, factory gate, MDA, etc.) is transfer- red via the Telepresence Box to the customer's network. For remote support, there must be an outgoing VPN connection from the customer network to the Telepresence Portal. The cus- tomer may be required to set up a firewall in the production net- work for security purposes. For condition monitoring, machine data is likewise transferred to TRUMPF via the customer's network. It belongs to the machine's scope of delivery. 3‐34 Industry 4.0 with TruConnect 2023-05-01 B1164en Universal interface for the Telepresence Box Central Link and OPC UA

Central Link consists of OPC UA Server and Device Gate. It is the interface via which the machine is networked with the cloud and cloud applications can be realized. This is based on the Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA), a standard of the OPC Foundation, that allows access to data and device functions. The Remote Control Interface (RCI) consists of a message and order interface. The production plan of the machine can be controlled directly via the order interface. This way, the machine can be connected to higher-ordered control systems or ERP/PPC systems, which can then load orders directly onto the machine. Thanks to the open architecture of the interface, the assignment and control can both be realized with TRUMPF systems such as Oseon, as well as with systems from other manufacturers. The message interface outputs production data of the machine in real time, thereby making system monitoring possible, e.g., with Oseon Analytics. 5.5 Remote support Remote support is established between the machine and a Tech- nical Service employee at TRUMPF via the telepresence portal. This way, personnel can be supported on site via remote control. Thanks to remote diagnostics, errors in practically all control components can be detected and remedied. 2. Operating the BendMaster 2.1 Safety information Workpiece is suspended from the suction cup of the BendMaster! The workpiece can fall down if the power supply is discon- nected or if the vacuum is reduced. Ø Only turn off the MAIN SWITCH and the compressed air supply if no workpiece is suspended from the vacuum grip- per of the BendMaster. Tools (grippers) are connected to the BendMaster, with frictional traction and form-locking, via a pneumatically actuated coupling system. Component failure or operating error can cause grippers to detach from the coupling and fall. Risk of injury! Ø When standing in the cell, keep at least 2 m distance from the BendMaster. If the compressed air fails, an error message is displayed in manual mode and the system stops. If these error messages are acknowledged, the system will still run in order to put the workpiece down. It will also emit an audible warning signal and display a message on the HMI. Unexpected drop in pressure at the gripper of the BendMaster while a workpiece is clamped! Risk of injury due to workpiece falling down. Ø If an acoustic warning signal is emitted, exit the processing cell immediately and close the safety doors. Ø Acknowledge messages. Ø Also during maintenance and cleaning work before entering the safety cabin: move the BendMaster manually and set down the clamped workpiece safely. Run-in procedure ■ The press brake is started. ■ The press program is loaded by the industrial PC. ■ The tools and backgauge of the TruBend are clamped and positioned. ■ The gripper used is fitted on the BendMaster if it has not been fitted yet. ■ Fine recognition is carried out on the stack. ■ If double sheet recognition was activated, double sheet rec- ognition and double sheet separation are performed. ■ The bending program is executed. ■ Finished sheets are set down on the unloading stack. The points within a path that the BendMaster moves along when approaching and traveling are referred to as calibration points and programmed in the offline system. There are two ways of editing such calibration points: ■ Teaching a point: − The desired position of the marked point is approached manually and saved as a new position. ■ Editing a point: − The position is changed by changing the coordinates manually in the respective coordinate system. Conveying unit is the umbrella term for all three conveying options (pallet conveyor, conveyor belt, chain conveyor). 1. Multi-gripper M The multi-gripper M is suitable for parts with a maximum weight of 52 kg (when used with BendMaster (60) - max. 38 kg). For workpieces not gripped at their center of gravity, the unequal load of the individual suction cups must be taken into account. Only the SAXM 60, 80, 100, 115 and SAB 60, 80, 100 suction cups from the company Schmalz approved by TRUMPF are per- mitted for the multi-gripper M. The suction cup type as well as the number and size of the suction cups must be selected according to the workpiece and the workpiece weight . 1.1 Description Design: The multi-gripper M is a gripping tool for the BendMaster (60) and BendMaster (150). It has a maximum of 8 suction cups whose position in the working area can be freely adjusted. The 8 suction cups can be switched on and off individually. This allows the multi-gripper M to manipulate a wide range of sheet metal bending parts. The 8 suction cups sit on 4 cross arms (referred to hereafter simply as "arms"), each of which carries 2 suction cups. The arms can be moved in the X direction. The 2 suction cups on each arm are coupled in the X direction. Each suction cup can be freely set in the Y direction in the working area. The quick-change coupling for the gripper and the valve terminal for individual shut-off are located on the underside of the multi- gripper. The vacuum sensor checks the vacuum quality and signals when there is not enough vacuum. 8‐2 Multi-gripper M 2023-05-01 B1164en

A933EN_SZ 2D mode: rotational solid 2-41 Locked Top View When working with pure 2D geometries, the display is automatically locked in the top view. An accidental turning of the view and associated construction faults are prevented. By converting a 2D geometry in a 3D geometry (thickening-up), spinning the construction and all 3D views are automatically enabled again. 2D-construction: ▪ Plan view locked ▪ No spinning possible 3D-construction: ▪ plan view not locked ▪ Spinning possible In the sheet metal ribbon under display the top view can be disabled/enabled manually.

A933EN_SZ Creating 3D drawings 2-42 9 Creating 3D drawings In the 3D mode, a solid can be created in the Sheet Metal area or in the Design area. Which variant is more suitable depends on the geometry to be created. 3D Sheet Metal Design Reduced selection of sketch tools. Every closed contour is automatically converted into a solid (3D). The entire design remains two-dimensional and must be thickened as required. If closed contours overlap, they are merged to form a single body. Overlapping is retained and can be split up as required. Patterns can only be created from simple geometries, that must be available as holes (3D). The pattern reference is retained. Even complex geometries can be used to create patterns. However, the pattern reference is lost as soon as you switch to 3D mode. Note: To be able to draw with construction lines in the 3D mode, the cut geometry must be displayed.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-52 11 Programming texts 11.1 Creating texts Texts are created with the Note tool on annotation planes created for this purpose. Procedure: 1. Open a new or existing part in TecZone Design. 2. Switch to Detail area and activate the Note tool. 3. Select the face on which the text is to be placed (The annotation plan is created automatically). 4. Place the note field. 5. Enter text or insert a dynamic field via the mini-toolbar. Note: The note field can be moved and/or rotated subsequently.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-53 11.2 Modifying texts A text must be selected to be subsequently changed. Font size: For the font size, it is relevant, which space is active in the properties Example: font size 3,5 View space: Model space: The text size is determined in relation to the size of the construction. Font type: To create a text as embossing text (EasyType), the font type must be adjusted in the properties. The text size iss et in the unit of measurement used in TruTops Boost.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-54 11.3 Marking texts The programming of an engraving is possible for written notes as well as for any geometries. Presetting for marking In DataManager Design is set whether a text to be marked is automatically converted to the font type ISO or whether the font with which it was created in TecZone Design is used.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-55 Programming marking Example: rectangle 100mm x100mm, any contours and text Option 1: 1. Create a new part in HomeZone. 2. Switch to TecZone Design. 3. Draw a rectangle, any lines and written notes.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-56 4. Switch to the 2D Technology area. 5. Select the desired elements. 6. Select Mark. 7. Validate and save the geometry. Note: The processing type of the selected object can be checked and changed in the properties.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-57 Option 2: 1. Create a new part in HomeZone. 2. Switch to TecZone Design. 3. Switch to Design area. 4. Draw a rectangle, any lines and written notes. 5. Select elements to be marked. 6. In the properties change the color to yellow. 7. Switch to Sheet Metal area. 8. Assign material 9. Validate and save the part.

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-58 11.4 Cutting texts TruTops Boost not only provides the option of engraving a text, but also of cutting it. For this, it may be necessary to prepare the text that it is suitable for a laser or punching processing. Procedure: 1. Create a new part (in the example, a rectangle of 100mm x 50mm). 2. Switch to the Detail area and select Note. 3. Position a note field, enter text and, if necessary, change the font. Note: The TC Laser and TC LaserSans fonts have already been prepared for punching / laser processing:

A933EN_SZ Programming texts 2-59 Option 1: 1. Select selection tool. 2. In the structure tree, right-click on note and determine whether to cut (cutout) or mark (engraving). Option 2: 1. Switch to the 2D Technology area. 2. Under Marking select the processing type Cut.

A933EN_SZ Special processing 2-60 12 Special processing 12.1 Hatching TruTops Boost offers the possibility to mark the outer contour of a surface, but also to hatch an area. Procedure: 1. Open the desired part in TecZone Design. 2. Select the surface. 3. Switch to 2D technology area. 4. Activate Hatch. Note: ▪ The hatching can be adapted and changed in the properties. ▪ Notes can not be hatched, they must first be projected onto the surface as a geometry.

A933EN_SZ Special processing 2-62 12.2 Dot marking points To generate dot marking points, markers must be placed and then be provided with the processing type marker. Procedure (example BP_72.GEO): 1. Open the desired part in TecZone Design. 2. Choose the marker toll in the Sheet Metal area. 3. Place marker. 4. Choose the placed points. 5. A933EN_SZ Special processing 2-63 12.3 Removing a protective film In case of foiled sheets, this function can be used to facilitate the subsequent removal of a protective film. The protective film is evaporated (laser) or cut (punch) along the selected contour. Thus, the protective film can only be released within the selected area. The rest of the sheet is still protected from scratches. Procedure: 1. Open file in TecZone Design. 2. Switch to the 2D technology area. 3. Activate remove protective film. 4. Adapt the parameters if necessary. 5. Create a peeling contour. The peeling contour can be set either by clicking a start point, setting a start point and end point, or by selecting an already existing contour. Example: Click on existing contour.

A933EN_SZ Creating and integrating geometry templates 2-64 13 Creating and integrating geometry templates Geometry elements that are saved as template (VLG file) can be integrated into any drawings. 13.1 Creating user-defined templates Procedure: 1. Draw geometry (possible in the Design menu as well as in the menu Sheet Metal). 2. Switch to the area 2D technology and save template. Select the contour define the reference point confirm 3. Enter a suitable name and save it as a VLG file.

A933EN_SZ Creating and integrating geometry templates 2-65 13.2 Integrating user-defined templates In addition to creating and using templates, TruTops Boost also offers predefined templates that can be placed on a part Procedure: 1. Open or create a sheet metal part. 2. Under Punching tools activate 2D template. 3. Select the desired template and place it.

A933EN_SZ Creating and integrating geometry templates 2-66 13.3 Constructing with punching tolls With this function, individual strokes of punching tools can be placed on a part. Each punching tool is assigned a corresponding ID number so that the desired tool is automatically accessed during the subsequent processing. Procedure: 1. Open an existing drawing or create a new part. 2. Choose the desired punching tool, adapt the options. 3. Place the punching tool. Note: If the selected tool is not available in TecZone Cut, the contour is not edited. In this case the association must be removed by right-clicking on the contour in TecZone Design.

A933EN_SZ Defining the upper machining side 2-67 14 Defining the upper machining side Which side of the part faces upwards during processing, e.g. on a laser or punching machine, is defined automatically when TruTops Boost creates the unfolding. An adjustment may be necessary if the part is equipped with a film, if the surface needs to be scratch-free or if an engraving is planned. Procedure: 1. Open part in TecZone Design. 2. Click on a surface and define it as the upper side. 3. Validate geometry and, if necessary, carry out further machining processing.

A933EN_SZ Presetting for importing 2D files 3-2 1 Presetting for importing 2D files External files can be imported into both HomeZone and TecZone Design. A933EN_SZ Presetting for importing 2D files 3-3 Recommended presetting: 2D data typically contain only geometry data, but no bending information. That is why the definition of the bending lines is required after importing a DXF file, for example. To simplify the import, make the following presetting: ▪ Import calculation in HomeZone: ▪ Import calculation in TecZone Design: Carry out the conversion from 2D to 3D yourself (for a better control of the entire import process). Enable direct access to the import parameters (e.g. when opening DXF files). After the import the 2D file remains in the structure tree.

A933EN_SZ Importing GEO files 3-4 2 Importing GEO files Importing GEO files from TruTops CAD is normally uncomplicated. As GEO files already include bending data and may have a material, a cutting or bending program can be created directly Procedure: 1. Start the import in HomeZone in the Part area. 2. Select the desired file. 3. Enter any missing information. 4. If required, create bending or cutting program.

A933EN_SZ Importing other 2D files 3-5 3 Importing other 2D files TruTops Boost also allows the following 2D formats to be imported: ▪ DXF ▪ DWG Procedure: 1. Import the file in the Part area. (multiple selection possible with Ctrl key) 2. Define material, raw material, … 3. Open in TecZone Design and, if necessary, process geometry. ▪ MI ▪ IGS

A934EN_SZ Designing for production 1-3 2 Designing for production Depending on the subsequent processing method – in particular with regard to bending methods and bending tools, you must pay attention to rules that are relevant to production in the case of 3D design of sheet metal parts. You must ask yourself the following questions: ▪ Which materials and sheet thicknesses have bend allowances stored for them? ▪ Which bend radiuses are possible? ▪ Which bending tools are available? ▪ How high are the flanges of a box allowed to be? ▪ How short is a bending flange allowed to be? ▪ How close to a bend is a hole allowed to be?

A934EN_SZ Designing for production 1-4 2.1 Basic information Bend Deduction In the case of sheet metal processing from a three-dimensional design model to a two- dimensional blank, you must consider a bend allowance. It is possible to calculate this value using a DIN formula, for example. However, this result only returns a guide value and it often not suitable for practical applications. If you need highly precise bending, you must determine the bend allowances empirically using several test bends using the correct tools. Values already determined for the respective tool combination are stored in the TruTops Boost database. These values are available to programmers at design and unfolding. Example: Material: 1.0038, s=2mm Bending: 90° air bending method Upper tool: radius 1mm Lower tool: die width 12mm, angle 30°, radius 1mm

A934EN_SZ Designing for production 1-5 Bend radius / production radius It is only possible to implement the desired bend radius (inside radius) at part production if the tools that are needed for this are present on the bending machine. A combination of the material, the material thickness, the upper tool radius and the die properties is responsible for the production radius that results in the bending process. The radius to be produced for the selected material is stored in the TruTops Boost data and is implemented in TruTops Boost Design during construction and unfolding. Example: Material: 1.0038, s=2mm Bending: 90° air bending method Upper tool: radius 1mm Lower tool: die width 12mm, angle 30°, radius 1mm 1 Upper tool (punch) 5 Die width (W) 2 Workpiece 6 Upper tool radius 3 Inside workpiece radius (Ri) 7 Lower tool radius 4 Die angle 8 Lower tool (die) 1 4 2 3 6 8 7 5

A934EN_SZ Designing for production 1-6 Die width In standard cases, the die width to be selected is about (6 - 8) x the sheet thickness. The bend deduction and radii resulting from a combination of the die and the upper tool are stored in TruTops Boost and you can use them for the design process. The die width affects parts production as follows: ▪ Small die width = small bend radius at increased bending force. ▪ Large die width = large bend radius at low bending force. Note: The die width (W) stated by TRUMPF is the dimension between the feed radiuses of the die. Other machine manufacturers generally define the dimension (W1) between the tangent intersection points. Nesting height If you are bending boxes, the sides that have already been bent can collide with the machine's beam. This means that the respective manufacturing limits must be complied with. If adapters (tool extensions) are available on the bending machine, you can carry out manufacturing with a greater nesting height. The limits below apply to TRUMPF standard upper tools: Upper tool height in mm Maximum nesting height in mm 120 65 140 78 220 131 240 145 Shi = Box height (inside) [mm] OWH = Upper tool height [mm] B = Press beam center to outside edge of the beam = 24 mm

A934EN_SZ Designing for production 1-7 Side length To ensure that it is possible to safely bend a bending flange, you must comply with a specific minimum length for it. Bending flanges that are too short slip into the die, which leads to undesirable deformation in the area of the bend zone. With a 90° bend, you can calculate the minimum length (b) of a bending flange using the following Formula: b = 0.75 x W (die width) Influence of the bend zone In the case of workpieces, which when unfolded, have a hole or a notch close to the bending line, you must keep a minimum distance from the bending edge so that no deformation of the contour occurs. A quick and workshop-oriented method of determining the minimum distance corresponds to calculation of the minimum flange length. If there are still contours present that are closer to the bend zone, or the bending flanges are too short or too angled, you must comply with specific design rules, like inserting bend reliefs or relief slots, for example. Die width Minimum side length 10 mm 7.5 mm 12mm 9mm 20 mm 15mm Wrong design Correct design You can calculate the minimum distance (X1) of a contour using the following formula: X1 = 0.75 x die width Design of workpieces in the area of the bend zone. A934EN_SZ Designing for production 1-8 Bend relief You frequently cut out bend zones regardless of whether two edges abut at a corner or a bending link plate is bent upward from a metal sheet surface. This gives you better corners and more scope when selecting and aligning bending tools. There are several options for cutting out bend zones. Using a punching machine, you usually generate round or rectangular holes at the start and end of the bending edge. Using a laser, you can also cut more complex bend relief contours. Examples: Round bend relief Square bend relief (standard) Laser bend relief

A934EN_SZ Preparing part geometries for manufacturing 4-60 11.3 Replacing slitting contours Contours that are narrower than the laser kerf lead to difficulties in the subsequent processing. Such contours should be converted into open contours. If these contours are oblong holes or rectangles, TruTops Boost Design makes it possible to automatically replace the narrow contours with slots. These are then cut as open contours. Replacing slitting contours manually Procedure (Example BD_40.scdoc): 1. Import file in HomeZone and open it in TecZone Design. 2. Choose the function Replace slitting contours. 3. Adjust options, if necessary. 4. Click on contours to be replaced.

A934EN_SZ Preparing part geometries for manufacturing 4-61 Replacing slitting contours automatically If narrow contours are to be automatically replaced by open contours, this presetting must be made in the Data Manager Design. Procedure (Example BD_40.scdoc): 1. Open the Data Manager Design or Design Options. 2. Activate automatic replacement of slitting contours. 3. Import file into HomeZone and open it in TecZone Design, if necessary. Note: An automatic set red frame around the replaced slot contour releases the geometry, even if cutting contours overlap or inner contours are protruding from the drawing.

A934EN_SZ Preparing part geometries for manufacturing 4-62 11.4 Bending zone margins suitable for punching Using the function simplify bending zone margins, the bending zone margins are smoothed in such a way that they consist of a maximum of two elements. Activate simplification of bending zone margins. 3. Import file into HomeZone and open it in TecZone Design, if necessary. before: afterwards:
